slices.name: Scope committee and meeting operations with atomic governance evidence
limitations: No RLS activation or partner audience change. Existing identity-reference validation is preserved; full ISO-04 reference governance and remaining controllers stay open.

slices.name: Scope governance document and poll artifacts with atomic evidence
Scope existing community governance visibility and audience transactions
Scope existing election policy and electorate snapshot transactions
Scope existing election procedure/privacy evidence and enforce latest policy
Scope existing election hold lifecycle and readiness transactions
Scope existing ballot review, draft and decision evidence transactions
Verify PostgreSQL pooled tenant context concurrency and SQL-error rollback
limitations: Test-only database context regression slice. No runtime RLS policies, tenant enforcement, new permissions or partner audience activation. ISO-01 through ISO-07 remain open.

slices.name: Scope existing privacy consent records, representative validation and append-only history to society transactions
limitations: No consent feature redesign, API changes, new permissions, schema/RLS policy or partner audience. This closes the consent subpath only; privacy requests, workers, other isolation batches and RLS remain open.

slices.name: Scope privacy registry categories, processors, and evidence to tenant transactions
limitations: No schema/RLS policy or entitlement/permission changes. Preserves category and processor workflows, response behavior and append-only audit evidence. Other privacy, worker and isolation areas remain open.

slices.name: Tenant-context privacy case intake, operator lists and parent-gated history, retaining independent-home requests
limitations: Only society case intake, listing and case/event history are converted; self-service and platform privacy cases remain independent-home-capable. Status, legal-hold, retention, subject-data erasure, readiness and reporting paths require separate review. No schema/RLS, permission, brand, endpoint or productionization change.

slices.name: Transaction-local lock and revalidation of privacy case status, legal hold, and retention review
limitations: Only status, legal-hold and retention-review lifecycle mutations are converted. Privacy program readiness, reporting, erasure, worker paths, and database RLS remain separate slices. Independent-home case workflows remain unscoped without fabricated society IDs. No schema, API contract, new authorization, partner activation or productionization changes.

slices.name: Scope privacy program readiness, evidence reporting and per-case readiness to society transactions
limitations: Only programReadiness, programEvidence and caseReadiness are converted. Reporting still uses default PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED transaction semantics; no repeatable-read guarantee or RLS activation. Other privacy context, self-service, erasure, worker and multi-partner isolation slices remain open. No schema, API, permission or productionization change.

slices.name: Tenant-scope privacy self-service requests, consent context, and operator subject audiences
limitations: No change to public controller guards or society-selection semantics. Requests without a society retain an unscoped transaction; the globally unique per-user request key remains unchanged across contexts. Platform society-null queue stays unscoped and filtered. This establishes tenant context, not database RLS or proof of statutory privacy compliance. Other subject-data and worker isolation, RLS and productionization remain open.

slices.name: Tenant-scope privacy subject-data exports and erasure planning/execution while preserving independent-home workflows
limitations: RLS remains disabled; setting tenant transaction context is a migration toward defense in depth and explicit SQL society/subject predicates remain mandatory. Erasure preflight and locked execution remain separate transactions; rechecks and row locks in the execution transaction are retained. No change to data minimisation categories, legal-hold/retention rules, endpoints, permissions, cross-society login guards or productionization.

slices.name: Tenant-context privacy incident and grievance access with locked incident lifecycle
limitations: Society-scoped incident and grievance workflows only; no separate society-less incident endpoint. Transaction-local society context does not activate database RLS. Incident disclosure policies, regulatory processes, external processors and production integrations are not broadened. Existing controller permissions and audit event types retained.

slices.name: Targeted workforce leave tenant isolation and concurrent overlap closure
limitations: V5.2.24 is a targeted workforce-leave slice informed by inspection of existing workforce services; not a claim that all inventory findings are closed. Workforce ratings, suspensions, general staffing, gate integration, and cross-partner controls need separate review. Transaction-local society context does not activate RLS. No schema, API, permission, independent-home, hardware integration, staging/main promotion or productionization change.

slices.name: Tenant-scope workforce rating and suspension actions with serialized status transitions and audit rollback
limitations: Scope is ratings and suspension only; not all workforce routes. Explicit society and active-occupancy guards retained; tenant context does not enable RLS. Worker and assignment suspension events retain existing audit table semantics. No controller permission, API, database schema, hardware integration, staging/main branch, or productionization change.

slices.name: Core workforce reviewer and resident mutation isolation with tenant-context gate visibility
limitations: Scope is core workforce review, deactivation, resident status and gate eligibility list; no replacement of existing serializable gate mutation path. Remaining workforce creation, payroll recording, attendance, cross-partner enforcement, broader RLS and productionization reviewed separately. Explicit society and UnitOccupancy filters preserved.

slices.name: Cross-society operational RBAC fail-closed checks and partner authority separation
limitations: Does not create partner portal or commercial partner APIs. Existing society membership and auth repository remain authoritative, session and gate SoD remain unchanged. This adds fail-closed request-boundary checks and two-partner PostgreSQL evidence; RLS and productionization out of scope.

slices.name: Workforce creation, private payment and attendance data access isolation
limitations: Scope is workforce household creation, payment record/attendance visibility and idempotent recording only; contract and existing gate serializable path remain unchanged. Commercial partner RBAC and independent-home requests not extended; tenant context does not activate RLS. Productionization and staging/main changes excluded.

slices.name: Final gate check-in authorization revalidation and V5.2 audience isolation regression/closure evidence
limitations: RLS remains disabled and is a separately tracked defense-in-depth enablement, not asserted here. Existing worker attendance/payments still rely on explicit society and occupancy predicates. No partner portal, external payment providers, physical access hardware, or productionization. Staging/main stay untouched. Final milestone status must be reconciled after protected CI merge.

slices.name: Runtime society branding contract, immutable revision persistence and authenticated read resolution
limitations: This slice does not expose draft/publish or image upload endpoints. The public bootstrap remains Aaraagate. Only validated, published society presentation can override the authenticated context response; no partner/distribution/host selection is introduced. No entitlements, roles, CSS/HTML, physical gate or finance behavior changed. RLS, productionization, staging/main promotion remain separate.

slices.name: Society-brand authoring, optimistic revision control and atomic publication
limitations: Only society presentation fields; no brand asset upload, media URL, custom CSS, partner distribution or portal host. No new entitlement or identity grants; management requires current operational SOCIETY_CONFIGURATION_MANAGE permission. Publishing is an immutable draft timestamp transition and history remains capped at 100 rows; rollback via future new revision, not mutating published record. No productionization, RLS or staging/main promotion.

slices.name: Shared Dart runtime society-brand contract and Resident/Guard theme adapters
limitations: This slice supplies a common validated presentation model and optional theme adapters; the current MaterialApp defaults remain unchanged until an authenticated context loader is explicitly wired in the next slice. No storage/caching, logos, native APK label/icon, partner host, billing, entitlements or operational authority changes.

slices.name: Resident authenticated society brand loader and stale-context-safe theme lifecycle
limitations: No persistent or cross-society offline brand cache. Failed config request uses the exact default Aaraagate theme; no login denial/entitlement effects. Demo, independent-home and signed-out contexts never fetch. Guard runtime fetching, Admin browser CSS, asset upload and rollback remain separate V5.3 slices.

slices.name: Guard runtime society-brand fetch and session-scoped presentation lifecycle
limitations: Uses existing API authenticated society context; presentation only. No persistent offline cross-society branding cache; demo/default, login failures or network errors retain built-in Guard theme and never block gate operations. Native app identity, logos, signed assets, web CSS/metadata and brand editor remain separate.

slices.name: Admin scoped runtime society-brand palette and client metadata
limitations: Branding is applied to the authenticated AdminConsole shell only and never to SSR root metadata or unauthenticated login. Dynamic colors must meet AA white-text contrast; unsafe colors use built-in default. Does not add admin brand editing UX, asset upload, verified hosts, partner white label, a persistent offline cache, RLS or productionization.

slices.name: Admin society-brand editor with safe preview, versioned drafts and publish actions
limitations: Only existing SOCIETY_CONFIGURATION_MANAGE management API routes are used. Operational permissions, finance, legal issuer, default login branding, native Android identity, partner portal, media upload, domain binding and RLS remain unchanged. The editor is exposed only to society/super administrators with backend reauthorization; individual tabs are not new authority. No staging/main promotion or productionization.

slices.name: Immutable society branding appearance restoration using versioned draft and publish lifecycle
limitations: Restore is a two-request opt-in workflow that leaves an unpublished draft if interrupted after draft creation; the UI surfaces that explicitly and requires reload. Existing server publication conflict checks remain authoritative. Only prior published society revisions are restorable; drafts and newer/current revisions cannot be treated as rollback targets. No new server authorization, schema, partner portal, media upload, native binary changes, productionization, RLS or staging/main promotion.

slices.name: Admin society palette accessibility parity with Resident and Guard using adaptive foreground tokens
limitations: Presentation-only Admin consistency: does not add image/logo storage, custom hostnames, offline brand persistence, partner distributions or native Android identity. No changes to backend brand publication, society RBAC, legal issuer, payment, guard gates, RLS or productionization. Scoped CSS variables never apply to login/SSR metadata and staging/main are unchanged.

slices.name: Resident and Guard foreground society-brand refresh with stale-response and offline safeguards
limitations: Only presentation on authenticated foreground resume; no periodic push channel, persistent cross-society cache, image/logo asset, distribution-specific branding or native Android packaging. Offline refresh failures preserve only a previously validated theme for the exact current session; signing out or switching societies synchronously clears it. No auth, gate data, server entitlement, schema, production infrastructure, RLS or staging/main change.

slices.name: Safe runtime society-branded support contacts across API, shared Dart and Admin editor
limitations: Only authenticated society support email and E.164 phone; no arbitrary URLs, mail sending or call triggering, partner distribution, media upload/logo rendering or independent-home society branding. Cosmetic fields never become authorization, legal issuer or entitlement values. Existing default public bootstrap and native application identity unchanged. RLS, infrastructure and staging/main promotion excluded.

slices.name: Private society PNG logo acquisition, bounded parser, ClamAV quarantine and society permissions
limitations: No logo publication, Admin/Flutter rendering, public image URL or native Android binary changes; asset revision binding is a separate V5.3.13 slice.
Real upload confirmation requires configured private object storage and ClamAV; infrastructure, productionization and hosted data remain outside scope.
Staging and main untouched; this slice requires protected CI gates before develop merge.

slices.name: Admin private PNG logo acquisition and malware-review workflow
limitations: Logo remains quarantined. Immutable revision linkage, protected image-delivery endpoint and mobile/Admin rendering are not enabled in this slice.
Direct signed PUT requires a configured private object store with Admin-origin CORS; no infrastructure setup, public logo URL, identity/entitlement change, staging or main promotion.

slices.name: Versioned branding revision accepts same-society VERIFIED logo reference only
limitations: Server validates logo ownership and verified status at draft/publish; no public/bootstrap/context image URL and no image bytes or rendering yet.
Admin/Flutter consumer image delivery and preview require a separate secured V5.3.15 slice.
No new tenant, roles, entitlements, storage migration or staging/main promotion.

slices.name: Authenticated current-published society logo PNG delivery with integrity verification
limitations: Returns bytes only under current society authentication and verified immutable publication, no signed GET/public CDN or direct arbitrary ID access.
No Resident/Guard/Admin image consumption in this slice; V5.3.16 required for scoped UI with default fallback.
Private store configuration and real-world infrastructure remain outside scope; no main/staging promotion.

slices.name: Verified Admin society-logo selection in immutable revisions and authenticated published preview
limitations: Only verified metadata is selectable; backend independently checks society ownership and verification on draft/publication.
Browser uses current authenticated PNG bytes and ephemeral blob URL; mobile Resident/Guard image presentation is V5.3.17.
No native app identity/host, partner role, gate/finance changes, staging/main promotion or production infrastructure.

slices.name: Session-scoped Resident/Guard PNG logo display with secure reuse and fallback
limitations: Mobile in-memory image only; no public/CDN URL, image persistence, new packages, native APK identity, hardware or productionization changes.
Already authenticated and scoped GET /context/logo remains the sole server authority; a missing/invalid logo leaves built-in Aaraagate presentation.
No role, entitlement, finance, guard workflow, staging or main changes.

slices.name: Mobile published-logo transport security and response timeout hardening
limitations: Remote mobile logo delivery requires HTTPS; cleartext localhost/loopback/Android emulator hosts remain permitted for local development only.
Response size, MIME, published-society authorization, PNG digest and file integrity continue to be validated by the existing backend; mobile maintains in-memory scope isolation.
No staging/main changes, production host configuration, native APK identity, role/permission/entitlement, gate or finance logic changes.

slices.name: Accessible society-logo presentation and immutable published-revision restore parity
limitations: Branding name/logos are cosmetic, session/society scoped and only obtained through existing authorized presentation flows.
Restoring an earlier appearance publishes a NEW immutable revision; backend verified-asset and owner permission gates are not bypassed.
No native identity, partner branding distribution, new infrastructure, external image URL, role, entitlement, finance or gate workflow changes.
No staging/main promotion. Full V5.3 closure requires CI and cross-society/rollback evidence.

limits: CI green is repository-based and does not prove live private-object-store/ClamAV/DNS/TLS/device rollout.
Partner-owned domains, licensing, Android distributions, and productionization remain future milestones.

milestones.name: Partner portal licensing and domain contracts

slices.name: Pure partner commercial license contract: bounded UTC/grace/capacity checks and non-granting feature ceilings
limitations: Policy calculation is not connected to existing production entitlements or login/guard actions; legacy Society.productTier and boolean overrides remain authoritative.
Capacity computation is a preview, not a reservation or enforcement; transactional licensing grant models, idempotency and platform role checks remain pending.
Commercial price/grace terms are not assumed; no partners/domains activated, no production infrastructure or staging/main change.

slices.name: Shared hostname canonicalization, reserved-domain denial and verified-only presentation candidate contract
limitations: No live DNS lookups, TXT challenge verification, partner portal routing, TLS, cookie changes or domain activation.
A registered/verified hostname supplies a cosmetic routing candidate only; it cannot grant partner/society permissions or access to data.
Existing legacy entitlements and society isolation remain unchanged; CI and safe partner-scoped API integration are separate gates.

slices.name: Commercial plan revisions and DRAFT-only partner license grant/audit persistence with Super Admin endpoints
limitations: Commercial revisions and audit events are immutable at the DB layer. New grants are DRAFT only; DB constraint rejects GRANTED or REVOKED until separately reviewed V5.4.5 activation.
Only existing platform SUPER_ADMIN sessions may create plan revisions or grant drafts. No partner portal authorization or partner self-service is enabled.
Existing Society.productTier, featureOverrides and EntitlementService.current remain authoritative. No change to gate, SOS, billing, finance or resident feature access.
No real-world pricing/grants, migrations applied to live environments, production infrastructure or staging/main promotion.
